So if we don't really need them, why do we have them? Well, the answer that most experts give is that we may not need them now, but our ancestors did. That's because they ate tough, uncooked foods—things like meat, plants, and nuts. So having wisdom teeth helped them grind the foods down to make them easier to eat. Of course, now we cook many of these tougher foods to make them softer, so we don't need to work so hard with our teeth. And over time, our jaws have become smaller.
